title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting and notation. X is a smooth connected projective variety of dimension n, polarized by an ample class xi_X in H^2(X), and L_X is cup product with xi_X. The primitive pieces are indexed by 0<=i<=2n:
- for i<=n, P^i(X) is the usual primitive part of H^i, i.e. the bottoms of the sl2-strings;
- for i>=n, P^i(X) = L^{i-n} P^{2n-i}(X) = Ker(L) in degree i, i.e. the tops of the strings;
- P^n is both a bottom and a top.
p_i^X denotes the projections onto these pieces. Lambda_X is Grothendieck's normalized Lambda (not the Kaehler/Hodge one with scalar factors): it is the degree -2 inverse of L along each string, and it kills the bottoms. Y is a smooth hyperplane section, xi_Y = phi^* xi_X, and phi: Y -> X is the inclusion.

A) Kernels and images.
- Im L = everything except the bottoms; Ker L = the tops.
- Im Lambda = everything except the tops; Ker Lambda = the bottoms.
Hence p_i L = 0 and Lambda p_i = 0 for i<=n, L p_i = 0 and p_i Lambda = 0 for i>=n, and in particular p_n commutes to 0 with both L and Lambda.

B) Lambda L = id - (sum of top projections); L Lambda = id - (sum of bottom projections). The crossed-out formulas 4'), 4'') were abandoned in favour of C).

C) Key formula 5): phi_* Lambda_Y phi^* = id - sum_{0<=i<=2n} p_i^X. That is, it is the identity on interior string elements and zero on bottoms and tops. Combined with 4), this gives Lambda L + L Lambda = T - p_n with T := id + phi_* Lambda_Y phi^* (formula (6)). Multiplying by L on both sides and using 3) yields
  7) L^2 Lambda + 2 L Lambda L + Lambda L^2 = L T + T L.

Corollary: A(X x X) and C(Y) imply C(X). Here 'C' in these notes evidently means 'Lambda is algebraic', i.e. the Lefschetz standard conjecture B of the 1968/69 numbering. The proof is implicit:
- View an operator u on H^*(X) as a correspondence class in H^*(X x X).
- u |-> L u + u L is cup product with xi⊗1 + 1⊗xi = L_{X x X}, so the left side of 7) is L_{X x X}^2 applied to the class of Lambda_X.
- That class lies in H^{2n-2}(X x X), and X x X has dimension 2n. So L^2: H^{2n-2} -> H^{2n+2} is a hard Lefschetz isomorphism.
- If Lambda_Y is algebraic, then T, and hence L T + T L, is algebraic.
- A(X x X), the inverse of the Lefschetz isomorphism preserving algebraic classes, then gives Lambda_X algebraic.

The marginal note sharpens this: one only needs A°(X x X), i.e. the statement in the single critical degree H^{2n-2} -> H^{2n+2}. The role of the result is the inductive reduction of the Lefschetz-type standard conjecture along hyperplane sections, which is the core of the 'standard conjectures' programme. The next page continues with the weak-Lefschetz comparison of primitive decompositions of X and Y.
errors: No genuine error found. Formula 5) checks string by string. For a in P^k with k<=n-1, phi^*a is primitive on Y with a string one shorter; phi_* Lambda_Y phi^* sends L^j a to L^j a for 1<=j<=n-k-1 and kills j=0 and j=n-k. For k=n, phi^*a=0 by injectivity of phi_* on H^n(Y). This uses weak Lefschetz/Gysin injectivity, which is not stated on the page.

The step 'A(X x X) gives C(X)' is left implicit. It needs the convention that left/right composition with L_X corresponds to cup product with pr_1^*xi resp. pr_2^*xi on correspondence classes, possibly up to transposition and sign conventions. It also needs the remark that phi_*, phi^* are algebraic correspondences (graph of phi).

The notation 'C(X)' here appears to denote algebraicity of Lambda (modern B(X)), not the Künneth conjecture C of the published numbering. The lettering in these notes evidently predates the 1968 numbering.

ideas.what: Normalized Lambda operator defined via the Lefschetz decomposition, with the indexing of primitive pieces P^i for 0<=i<=2n (bottoms and tops of sl2-strings), and the kernel/image calculus A), B)
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz operator Lambda (Grothendieck/Kleiman normalization), sl2/Lefschetz decomposition
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968, publ. 1969)

ideas.what: Identity phi_* Lambda_Y phi^* = id - sum p_i^X, hence Lambda L + L Lambda = id + phi_* Lambda_Y phi^* - p_n
ideas.modern_name: comparison of Lefschetz operators of X and a hyperplane section
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kleiman (Dix exposés 1968) in the proof that B(Y) helps to give B(X); unsure of the exact form

ideas.what: Formula L^2 Lambda + 2 L Lambda L + Lambda L^2 = L T + T L, read as L_{X x X}^2 [Lambda_X] being algebraic, giving: A(X x X) (even only in the critical degree 2n-2 -> 2n+2) together with B(Y) implies B(X)
ideas.modern_name: hyperplane-section reduction of the Lefschetz standard conjecture B
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kleiman 1968, Grothendieck 1969 (results of the type 'B(Y) and A(X x X) imply B(X)')
ideas.where_published: Probably close to statements in Grothendieck 1969 §4 and Kleiman 1968 §4; exact form unsure

missed.claim: Early, unpublished derivation of the hyperplane-section reduction for the Lefschetz standard conjecture, with an explicit operator identity. The marginal refinement shows only the critical-degree part A°(X x X) (L^2: H^{2n-2} -> H^{2n+2} on X x X) is needed. This documents the genesis of results later written up by Kleiman. It is probably not new mathematics, but the 'only critical degree' formulation may be sharper than commonly quoted statements.
missed.quote: On y peut remplacer A(X×X) par A°(X×X) (assertion "dans les dimensions critiques" H^{(2n)-2}→H^{(2n)+2})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Pins down the minimal Lefschetz input on X x X needed to propagate B up from a hyperplane section; of mainly historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean working sheet deriving a known reduction (B(Y) + A(X x X) implies B(X)), very likely matching Kleiman 1968 / Grothendieck 1969. The explicit identity and the critical-degree refinement are nice historical details but not unknown to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Formula 1): the superscript of the first p is a handwritten X over i, i.e. p_i^X.
'd'où compte tenu de 3*)' refers to formula 3), with the 3 rewritten by hand.

In 7) the middle term is hand-corrected to 2 L_X Λ_X L_X and the last term to Λ_X L_X^2. The right side is the handwritten 'L_X T_X + T_X L_X, avec T_X donné par (6)', and the crossed-out expansion of T_X is deleted.
The marginal note reads 'On y peut remplacer A(X×X) par A°(X×X) (assertion "dans les dimensions critiques" H^{(2n)-2} → H^{(2n)+2})'.
